note: A listening exercise for someone new: tap a note and then Do to hear home, tap the two chords that differ by one note, then name major or minor by ear and try it on a song. One staff per step, each showing only the notes that step names; the staff is explained the first time, and the game's answers are named as the buttons show them (M3, m3).

exercise.title: Home, and the note that makes major or minor
exercise.why: Do is the note a tune comes to rest on, and the 3rd above it decides major or minor, so these two sounds are the ones to learn by ear first.

cells.text: The staff below, the five lines of music, shows the C major scale with its solfège names: tap a note to hear it. Tap {{1}}, then {{7}}, and stop: it sounds unfinished. Tap {{1}} again and it comes home. Now try the other notes the same way: tap one, wait, then tap {{1}}.

cells.heading: One note makes major or minor

cells.text: Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} below: that's a C major chord, one note at a time.
Now tap {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}}: C minor. Only the middle note moved, down a half step. Go back and forth between the two staffs until you can tell them apart with your eyes closed.
Press Start in the game below. It plays two notes together: pick M3 for a major 3rd or m3 for a minor 3rd. Then put on a song you like and guess whether it is major or minor.
